comparison: Perfect alignment on electrophysiology data (C46-C51). Both evaluations support the findings, though peer reviewers noted a scope limitation (only layer II/III neurons measured) rather than challenging validity.

Strong agreement on SWD frequency data (C60-C65, C67). Both support the findings that mTORC2 inactivation provides partial protection while mTORC1 inactivation does not. OpenEval explicitly addresses C66 which peer reviewers discuss separately in R8.

Strong agreement on interictal EEG findings (C68-C73). Both evaluations support that dual inactivation is required to normalize most EEG features. OpenEval addresses incomplete rescue of relative power (C74) which peer reviewers discuss in R10.

Strong agreement on biochemical validation data (C33-C39). Both evaluations support the pathway-specific activation and rescue findings. OpenEval includes C87-C88 (methodological rationale) not explicitly addressed by peer reviewers.

Both evaluations rate as UNCERTAIN due to small sample sizes for seizure incidence data (C52-C57). Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge statistical limitations while accepting the main conclusion. OpenEval notes the 0/6 result is suggestive but not definitive. Both accept the study despite this limitation.

Agreement on histological data (C42-C45). Both support the findings on soma hypertrophy and cortical thickness. Peer reviewers also address C95 (hippocampal soma size) which OpenEval discusses in R10.

Strong agreement on main conclusions (C6-C8, C75-C78). Both support that dual inactivation is required to rescue epilepsy phenotypes. However, peer reviewers distinguish necessity vs. sufficiency in R12 regarding C8, noting conclusions may be overstated.

Agreement on therapeutic implications (C9, C85-C86). Both support recommendations for dual inhibition. OpenEval notes these are speculative claims requiring clinical validation; peer reviewers accept the therapeutic relevance based on the data.

Divergent evaluations of experimental model (C29-C32). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding appropriate methodological detail. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting hippocampal expression as a weakness/limitation, though concerns were addressed with additional data (C92-C94).

Both address off-target hippocampal expression (C92-C94). OpenEval supports the control data showing no relationship between hippocampal expression and seizures. Peer reviewers initially raised concerns but accepted after additional data, rating as UNCERTAIN overall.

Agreement on lack of correlation between pathway activity and seizure presence (C100, C103-C104). Both support these findings as addressing potential confounds. OpenEval also discusses additional control data (C96-C99, C101-C102) addressed separately by peer reviewers.

Partial overlap on seizure duration and pathway activity correlation (C97-C99). OpenEval groups these with other control data in R11. Peer reviewers address C58-C59 (seizure duration findings) in R6, supporting the observation that Raptor knockout aggravated seizure duration.
Agreement on mortality data (C101-C102). Both support these findings as evidence of phenotype severity and rescue effects. OpenEval notes mortality could not be linked to seizures due to timing.

Both address C66 (mTORC1 inactivation provides no protection). OpenEval includes this in broader SWD analysis (R6), while peer reviewers explicitly affirm this finding separately (R8), noting Raptor knockout did not prevent seizures.

Both address C74 (incomplete rescue of relative power distribution). OpenEval includes this in interictal EEG analysis (R7) noting unclear biological significance. Peer reviewers accept this finding (R10) as supporting nuanced conclusion about incomplete rescue.
Both address C77 (dual deletion rescues epilepsy). OpenEval includes this in main conclusions (R8). Peer reviewers accept this finding (R10) as part of the rescue data.

Divergent evaluation of C8 (both complexes cause epilepsy). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting conclusions are overstated - data show necessity but not sufficiency for causation.

Both address C6 (main conclusion about dual deletion requirement). OpenEval includes this in R8 as supported by convergent evidence. Peer reviewers address in R5, accepting main conclusion despite statistical limitations in seizure incidence data.

OpenEval evaluated background/literature claims (C1-C28, C40-C41, C81) as SUPPORTED, finding authors accurately represent established knowledge and prior research. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval rated mechanistic speculation (C79-C80) as UNCERTAIN, noting these interpretations are not directly tested and require validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific speculative mechanisms.
